paragraphs.en: 交互即裁判评估范式通过智能体直接与应用程序交互，提升了交互式应用程序的评估和生成效果。 Coding agents are tasked with producing sophisticated interactive applications such as websites, desktop applications, and games. While humans assess these applications interactively, current automated LLM evaluations primarily focus on code analysis and unit tests. This mismatch can cause LLM judges to miss failures that are immediately apparent to human users. We study Interaction-as-a-Judge, an evaluation paradigm where computer-use agents (CUAs) directly interact with an application. We demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can improve both evaluation and generation of interactive applications. To this end, we collect and release two complementary datasets: $6,858$ pairs of applications with human preferences and corresponding agent traces, and $222$ applications with human-verified requirement labels. Relative to standard non-interactive approaches, we find that Interaction-as-a-Judge improves evaluation in terms of predicting human preferences ($65.6\% \to 69.1\%$) and requirement verification ($77.0\% \to 81.6\%$). We also observe scaling benefits: across both preference alignment and requirement verification, higher-quality interactions improve performance. Finally, through both inference- and training-time experiments, we demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can also improve the quality of generated artifacts. At inference time, Interaction-as-a-Judge repairs $75.5\%$ of broken requirements within five attempts, compared to $55.4\%$ for code-only self-feedback. At training time, using Interaction-as-a-Judge as a reward signal improves win-rate over the base model by $6.7$pp while reducing both generated code length by $35.7\%$ and build failure rates by $7.2$pp compared to a code-only reward signal.
paragraphs.zh: 交互即裁判评估范式通过智能体直接与应用程序交互，提升了交互式应用程序的评估和生成效果。编码智能体的任务是生成复杂的交互式应用程序，例如网站、桌面应用程序和游戏。 虽然人类以交互方式评估这些应用程序，但当前的自动化 LLM 评估主要关注代码分析和单元测试。 这种不匹配可能导致 LLM 裁判忽略对人类用户而言显而易见的问题。 我们研究了“交互即裁判”（Interaction-as-a-Judge）这一评估范式，其中计算机使用智能体（CUAs）直接与应用程序进行交互。 我们证明，“交互即裁判”能够提升交互式应用程序的评估和生成效果。 为此，我们收集并发布了两个互补的数据集：包含 $6,858$ 对应用程序与人类偏好及对应智能体轨迹的数据，以及包含 $222$ 个经过人类验证的需求标签的应用程序。 与标准的非交互方法相比，我们发现“交互即裁判”在预测人类偏好（从 $65.6\%$ 提升至 $69.1\%$）和需求验证（从 $77.0\%$ 提升至 $81.6\%$）方面提升了评估效果。 我们还观察到扩展性优势：在偏好对齐和需求验证两方面，更高质量的交互都能提升性能。 最后，通过推理和训练阶段的实验，我们证明“交互即裁判”也能提升生成产出的质量。 在推理阶段，“交互即裁判”在五轮尝试内修复了 $75.5\%$ 的失效需求，而仅依赖代码自我反馈的修复率仅为 $55.4\%$。 在训练阶段，将“交互即裁判”用作奖励信号，使胜率相比基础模型提升了 $6.7$pp，同时生成的代码长度减少了 $35.7\%$，构建失败率降低了 $7.2$pp（与仅使用代码作为奖励信号的情况相比）。
